chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
From a man who married a woman and had intercourse with her, he said: 'Her dowry is obligatory, and she is forbidden to her father and her son.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the specific relatives of the husband to whom a consummated wife becomes permanently forbidden?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that consummation (dakhul) creates a permanent marital bond, rendering the wife forbidden to her husband's father and son, a ruling derived from the principle of 'marriage of the same degree.' The mention of the obligatory dowry underscores that the financial right is secured upon consummation, even if the divorce or death occurs subsequently, reflecting the juristic consensus on the efficacy of the contract's execution.
